title: Identity and Access

header.html: Describe directory services in Azure, including Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Entra Domain Services; Describe authentication methods in Azure, including single sign-on (SSO), multifactor authentication (MFA), and passwordless; Describe external identities in Azure; Describe Microsoft Entra Conditional Access; Describe Azure role-based access control (RBAC)
the official AZ-900 study guide, skills measured as of July 20, 2026

html:
1Authentication and authorization

Term Question it answers Example
Authentication Who are you? Proving your identity Signing in with a password and a code
Authorization What are you allowed to do? Permissions after sign-in Read-only access to a resource group
Exam tip

. Authentication first, authorization second. Microsoft Entra ID handles sign-in; RBAC decides what you may do with Azure resources.

2Directory services

Microsoft Entra ID is Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service. It stores users, groups and applications and signs people in to Azure, Microsoft 365 and thousands of other apps. Old name It was called Azure Active Directory (Azure AD); exam questions may still use the old name.

Microsoft Entra ID Microsoft Entra Domain Services
What it is Cloud identity service for sign-in and access to apps Managed domain services in Azure
Provides Single sign-on, MFA, app access, external identities, device registration Domain join, group policy, LDAP and Kerberos/NTLM authentication
Use it when You need cloud sign-in and app access Legacy apps need traditional domain features and you do not want to run your own domain controllers

Entra Domain Services gives a managed domain that is compatible with Windows Server Active Directory, so lift-and-shift apps that rely on LDAP, Kerberos or group policy work without you deploying and patching domain controllers.

A tenant is a dedicated instance of Microsoft Entra ID for an organization. A subscription trusts one tenant (Module 5).

3Authentication methods

Single sign-on (SSO)

SSO lets a user sign in once and access multiple applications and resources without signing in again, using one set of credentials. It reduces password fatigue and improves security.

Multifactor authentication (MFA)

MFA requires two or more kinds of proof (factors):

Factor Meaning Examples
Something you know A secret Password, PIN
Something you have A device or token Phone with authenticator app, security key
Something you are A biometric Fingerprint, face

A stolen password alone is not enough to sign in.

Passwordless authentication

Passwordless replaces the password with something stronger and easier. Options in Microsoft Entra ID:

  • Windows Hello for Business (biometric or PIN tied to the device).
  • Microsoft Authenticator app (sign in by approving a notification, with biometric or PIN).
  • FIDO2 security keys (a physical key).

Exam tip

. Password only is the weakest. MFA adds a second factor. Passwordless removes the password and is both convenient and secure.

4External identities

External identities let people outside your organization use your apps and resources with their own identity.

Scenario What it provides
B2B collaboration (business to business) Invite partners or guests to use your apps, signing in with their own organization or personal account
B2C / customer identities (business to consumer) Let customers sign up and sign in to your consumer apps with social or local accounts
Exam tip

. "Partners from another company need access to a SharePoint site" → B2B / guest users. "Customers sign in to our public app with their social account" → B2C / customer identity.

5Microsoft Entra Conditional Access

Conditional Access is a policy engine that makes if-then decisions at sign-in. It brings signals together and applies a decision.

Signals (if) Decisions (then)
User or group membership Block access
Location (country, IP range) Grant access
Device (compliant, managed) Grant but require MFA
Application being accessed Require a compliant or hybrid-joined device
Sign-in risk Require a password change or terms of use

Example: "If a user signs in from outside the country, then require MFA." Conditional Access needs a paid Entra ID license (P1 or higher). [Verify live]

6Azure role-based access control (RBAC)

Azure RBAC manages who has access to Azure resources, and what they can do with them. You create a role assignment, which has three parts:

Part Meaning
Security principal Who: a user, group, service principal or managed identity
Role definition What: a collection of permissions
Scope Where: management group, subscription, resource group or resource

Built-in roles (fundamental four):

Role What it can do
Owner Full access, including assigning roles to others
Contributor Create and manage everything, but cannot grant access to others
Reader View resources only
User Access Administrator Manage user access to resources, but not the resources themselves
  • Permissions are inherited from higher scopes to lower ones (Module 5).
  • Role assignments are additive: a user gets the combined permissions of all roles assigned.
  • Apply least privilege: give only the access needed, at the narrowest sensible scope.
Exam tip

. Owner can assign roles; Contributor cannot. Reader only views. RBAC controls Azure resources; Entra roles control Entra ID itself. Beyond the study guide

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors has a legacy app that needs LDAP and Kerberos, and it does not want to manage domain controllers. Which service fits?

  • AAzure DNS
  • BAzure Policy
  • CMicrosoft Entra Domain Services
  • DAzure Advisor
Show the answer

Answer: C. Entra Domain Services provides a managed domain with LDAP, Kerberos and group policy, without domain controllers to run.

S2A user signs in once and can then open several applications without entering credentials again. What is this?

  • AMultifactor authentication
  • BRole-based access control
  • CSingle sign-on
  • DConditional Access
Show the answer

Answer: C. SSO means one sign-in gives access to many applications.

S3A policy must require MFA only when users sign in from outside the country. Which feature does this?

  • AResource locks on the sign-in page
  • BAzure Cost Management reports
  • CVNet peering between two networks
  • DMicrosoft Entra Conditional Access
Show the answer

Answer: D. Conditional Access applies if-then rules using signals such as location.

S4An administrator needs to let a developer create and manage virtual machines in a resource group but not grant access to anyone else. Which role fits?

  • AContributor
  • BOwner
  • CReader
  • DUser Access Administrator
Show the answer

Answer: A. Contributor can create and manage resources but cannot assign roles. Owner can also assign roles.

S5A partner company's employees need access to one of your apps using their own accounts. What should you use?

  • AA new subscription for the partner company
  • BA VPN Gateway for each partner
  • CExternal identities (B2B guest users)
  • DA management group for guests
Show the answer

Answer: C. B2B collaboration lets guests sign in with their own identities.

S6Which is an example of passwordless authentication?

  • AA FIDO2 security key or Windows Hello for Business
  • BA password and a security question that the user chooses
  • CA much longer password with special characters
  • DA shared account for the whole team
Show the answer

Answer: A. Passwordless methods replace the password, for example with a security key, Windows Hello or the Authenticator app.

S7Which statement describes authorization?

  • AVerifying who a user is when they sign in
  • BEncrypting a disk with a key
  • CDetermining what a signed-in user is allowed to do
  • DChoosing a region for the resources
Show the answer

Answer: C. Authorization decides permissions; authentication verifies identity.

7.2 Recall questions

R1What is the new name of Azure Active Directory?

Show the answer

Microsoft Entra ID.

R2Name the three MFA factor types.

Show the answer

Something you know, something you have, something you are.

R3Which Azure RBAC role can assign roles to others?

Show the answer

Owner (and User Access Administrator).

R4What are the three parts of a role assignment?

Show the answer

Security principal, role definition and scope.

R5What does Entra Domain Services give you without domain controllers?

Show the answer

A managed domain with domain join, group policy, LDAP and Kerberos/NTLM.

R6Which feature uses signals to allow, block or require MFA?

Show the answer

Conditional Access.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Authentication vs authorization who you are vs what you may do
Entra ID cloud identity service (formerly Azure AD): SSO, MFA, app access
Entra Domain Services managed domain: join, group policy, LDAP, Kerberos; no domain controllers
SSO / MFA / passwordless one sign-in; two or more factors; no password (Hello, Authenticator, FIDO2)
External identities B2B guests and B2C customers
Conditional Access if-then at sign-in using signals (user, location, device, app, risk)
RBAC principal + role + scope; Owner, Contributor, Reader, User Access Administrator; inherited and additive
